title: How deep? Spend calculation where it pays
outcomes: Follows a forcing line to a quiet position before judging it
Tells critical moments from routine ones
Gives reasons to stop a line
Records how deep a line went and whether it was worth it

steps.text:
Depth is a **budget**, not a virtue. Habits to try:
**Go deep** when every move in the line is a check, capture or threat: the replies are few.
**Stop** when the position is quiet and you can compare it, when you have found a refutation, or when the clock says so.
**Spend more** at critical moments, less at routine ones.

steps.caption: White to move. Every move in the winning line is a check or a capture.

line.say: Rxh7+ gives up a rook. A short look stops here.

claims.statement: Rxh7+ is the engine's best move.

steps.text:
**Four stop signs:** the position is quiet; you found a refutation; no line changes the material (the moment is routine); time. And **two warning signs** that you stopped too early: your line ends on a capture, or on a check.
Depth allocation is a habit to try; nobody has measured the best split.

steps.title: Go deep, stop early, or stop
steps.prompt: Judge each: should the calculation go deep, would stopping early mislead, or is the moment routine? Predict, then check.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** There is no checklist panel in this lesson; the checklist is the card above, and hints are offered on each item. A silent item switches hints and the engine off. The plan is to offer hints only on request once you solve items like these without them. Next item is silent.

steps.prompt: Depth log for the silent item. Write how many plies your longest line had and whether the depth was worth it. This record is for you; it is not scored.
